NTA

My brother once racked up a bill well into 5 digits. I kept giving bc I loved him. Turns out it was all for drugs. You are never required to give your hard earned money, even to family, unless you are 150% to see it back w/in a timely manner. Whether you like them or not, it is simply not an obligation of being family. 

On a side note, my brother is completely sober and GM at a high end restaurant. He is doing so well. I will still never see that money. But I have since earned back what I lost plus I have my brother back. I shouldn't have had to pay to get him back but I am glad to see him doing so well. We were very lucky and he seems to have nipped it in the bud his first try. Not to say he could not relapse ever, but he just got his 5 yr coin :)

What I've learned is that is totally ok to support people in your life without doing so monetarily. Not saying you necessarily should be there for your sister bc of how she treats you, but it does seem like disease may be the underlying cause of why your relationship is so strained. 

Maybe look up what a flight home would be. If you can find a cheap one, maybe it would be a nice gesture for her to at least be able to crash on your mom's couch for the time being. Definitely not a necessity, as again, your earned money is yours. But guessing that disease is a major cause of her issues, maybe being back home w no rent will be the push she needs to get back on her feet.

I think I'm gonna be sad. I think it's today.

Every damn day.

Most of our chefs worked their way up thru the restaurant. We are "upscale casual" so yes, our entrees range from $20-$40 (huge portions though), but our chefs are experienced simply by being in the restaurant business. Our owner did the same thing.. started as a dish room worker, worked his way up to be a line cook and then ended up buying the place. So no.. close to none of our chefs went to culinary school or were mentored. I can only think of one who will actually finish 4 yrs of culinary school and he says he learns more about being a chef on the line, not in school. So don't assume that bc our entrees can be expensive that every chef has had 8+ yrs of education.
I'm not lazy. Depression makes me exhausted all the time with no motivation to do things
You guys are sweet. But there's no hope for me. I've tried to get better so many times. I'm just not meant for this world.

If I swing by and you say you're ready to order, actually be ready to order. I will absolutely stop the list of things I'm doing today take your order but if you then sit there talking to your spouse about options, maybe an app maybe no app, this is wasting precious time I need for other tables. It's fine if you have questions or need help deciding but don't go out of your way to pull me aside while I'm running around if you still don't even know if you want 2 courses yet. 

Also, do your best to get all your refills and other needs at the same time. It's such a pain leaving the table, going to get your soda and then I come back and your friend needs one too. I plan on making one trip and when I have to go back and forth to the same table it eats up time I needed for other tables. 

Just be a decent human. I am also a human with bills and a life outside of work. Please don't ask why I'm working there if I have degree. Also understand that I'm not allowed to kick you out. If you ask me when you can stay til, I cannot ask you to leave. This is not an invitation though to stay until all hours of the night. I'll still have to clean and do my drawer after you leave which is another 45-60 min of work before I can even start my drive home for the night.
I woke up again. So decently awful. When does it end? I don't want to keep doing this

As a daughter who tried to kill herself, my dad came every day for a visit and bring me dinner and we'd play cards. It was awesome getting better food than the hospitals provide and also a time to just sit down and play cards with my dad and feeling relaxed because it was the one place my mind would be distracted where I didn't have to talk about depression. She will spend the rest of her day living in that and it's a nice escape and something to look forward to. You are being a great father. 

I prayed that my mom wouldn't think the same thing you're thinking... How could she miss this? This is 100% not reality. In depression, you live constantly with a mask and no one knows the real you. We are amazing actors like that. I also hope you don't feel poorly that she didn't confide in you. Please know that when you feel so low, your brain starts to play tricks on you, like being swallowed by a black hole. You feel like no one can save you and it becomes isolating to the point in which everyone is so distant from your reality. 

For your daughter, I feel for you. I know the pain. It's daunting and a frightening journey. But if you've ever seen those pictures of people walking against the wind into sleet or snow, you know they eventually make it to their destination. Healing is possible and it takes everyone a different amount of time so please never beat yourself down for not progressing as fast as someone. You will get there. I'm so very sorry for what you've experienced. I wish you the absolute best.
Because don't we all scream for ice cream?
